concept: An agent that is a file and remembers between HTTP requests, in a directory the app chooses
triggers: where does agent memory get stored
notCovered: the React side — useAgent and rendering the stream
per-user memory stores and the owner check a real app needs
recall quality: whether the right fact is retrieved for a given question
memory poisoning and the permission layer — sdk/memory measures that

lessons.explains: A served agent keeps nothing between requests except what is on disk, and .memory() takes the SDK's MemorySettings unchanged — including where the store lives
Why 'public' costs more once an agent remembers: over a stateless agent it leaks a reply, over this one it leaks a history
A relative directory is refused rather than resolved, because 'relative to what' has two answers in a served app
The agent never decides to remember — a durable entry traces to the user's text, so a UI that never sends the instruction produces no entries
A state-changing route is CSRF-protected by default, so a hand-built request gets 403 before it reaches the agent

evidence.claims: Starts the real theokit dev with no credential and proves four things: an unknown agent is 404 while this one is 200; a durable memory lands in the declared directory and NOT in the SDK's default; and a fact learned in one request appears in the prompt the provider receives on the next
